questions.prompt: Which is an activity number, not an outcome?

options.explanation: This is an outcome. Meetings are a result for the business.
Right. It counts work done by the tool, not what changed for customers.
This is an outcome. It shows how recipients responded.

questions.prompt: Anthropic's cost guide says how to compare two models. How?

options.text: By the price per token on the vendor's price list.
options.explanation: The guide says price lists are per token, but you pay for completed tasks.
The guide says to measure cost per completed task on your own traffic.

options.text: By the cost per completed task.
options.explanation: Right. A stronger model can do less work per task, so its cost per task can be lower.

questions.prompt: Which is a limit of user feedback, according to Anthropic's post on evals?

options.text: It never shows problems that the team didn't expect.
options.explanation: The post lists the opposite as a strength: feedback surfaces problems you didn't anticipate.

options.text: It is sparse and self-selected, and rarely says why.
options.explanation: Right. The post also says it skews toward severe issues.

options.text: It costs too much to collect from customers at any size.
options.explanation: The post doesn't list cost as a limit of user feedback.
